cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery says your portrait needs a stronger likeness. Let's take that as a practical note.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They didn't recognize you, did they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Recognition depends on more than a face. Use the shirt I wore for the sitting as a reference; they need a clear identifying feature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I painted the shirt exactly. They asked why I'd put it on somebody else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the shirt is working. We'll bring the face into line with it. Start with the jaw; leave the part they recognized alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 softens non-recognition into a practical likeness note. A3 prescribes an identifying feature; B4's evidence that it already works lets A5 correct the remaining face as a manageable repair rather than repeat the hurtful judgment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks about recognition and A3 shifts to useful visual cues. B4 shows the shirt was recognized but the person was not, so A5 preserves the shirt and directs face revision.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the actual criticism and B4 supplies what the gallery said. A remains supportive while responding to the artist's knowledgeable correction.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's harsher assessment into a concrete division between successful and improvable work, deepening kindness through supervised action.

specificity.evidence: A1 gallery portrait and B2 A as sitter establish the task; B4 recognizable shirt explains A5's decision to leave that part alone.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's face/jaw instruction has a recipient and aim; it avoids an appended joke that would undercut the emotional support.
